title: Chromosomes 9 and X
clinical_history: Demonstration metaphase prepared for laboratory teaching. The recorded sex is female. The task is to separate chromosome 9 from the X chromosome. No clinical abnormality is provided.
unknown_prompt: Chromosome 9 and the X chromosome both sit in the C group. Pair each one by length and band pattern, then write the karyotype.

learning_rounds.title: 9 and X
learning_rounds.note: Chromosome 9 and the X both belong to the C group. This cell has two of each. Compare length and the band pattern before you accept a match.

plain_language_interpretation: A normal female diploid karyotype. Chromosome 9 and the X chromosome are both present as normal pairs.
diagnosis: No cytogenetic abnormality identified (normal female karyotype)
explanation: Chromosome 9 and the X chromosome are medium submetacentric chromosomes in group C. A female cell has two X chromosomes and two chromosomes 9. This demonstration cell has 46 chromosomes and no extra, missing, or rearranged chromosome.
hints: Both chromosomes belong in group C. Do not separate them by group letter alone.
Use relative length and the band pattern around the centromere.
A normal female study is written 46,XX when no further change is present.
